definitions_and_conventions: An Orlicz function ψ : [0,∞) → [0,∞) is convex and increasing, satisfies ψ(0)=0, and tends to infinity as its argument tends to infinity.
For an Orlicz function ψ, ‖X‖ψ = inf {t>0 : E ψ(|X|/t) ≤ 1}.
Lψ(Ω,Σ,P) is the space of random variables X with ‖X‖ψ<∞.
A random variable is sub-gaussian when it satisfies one of the equivalent properties (i)–(iv) of Proposition 2.5.2.
Equation (2.13) defines the sub-gaussian norm by inf {t>0 : E exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2}.
implicit_context: All expectations are taken with respect to P.
Random variables and function spaces carry the usual almost-everywhere identification, although the example does not restate that convention.
The word increasing is used in the standard Orlicz-function sense of order-preserving/nondecreasing.
The norm comparison uses P(Ω)=1, so E[1]=1.

details: ψ₂ is increasing and convex on [0,∞).
ψ₂(x) tends to infinity as x tends to infinity.
Because P is a probability measure, E[exp(X²/t²)−1]≤1 is equivalent to E exp(X²/t²)≤2.
Therefore the admissible positive scales in the Orlicz norm and in equation (2.13) are identical, so their infima are exactly equal.
X belongs to Lψ₂ exactly when the common Orlicz/sub-gaussian norm is finite.
By Definition 2.5.6 and Proposition 2.5.2(iv), this is exactly the class of sub-gaussian random variables.
Property (i): there is K₁>0 such that P{|X|≥t}≤2 exp(−t²/K₁²) for all t≥0.
Property (ii): there is K₂>0 such that ‖X‖Lp≤K₂√p for all p≥1.
Property (iii): there is K₃>0 such that E exp(λ²X²)≤exp(K₃²λ²) whenever |λ|≤1/K₃.
Property (iv): there is K₄>0 such that E exp(X²/K₄²)≤2.
The source declares these four properties equivalent and defines sub-gaussianity by satisfaction of any one of them.
ψ₂ is the selected Orlicz function; the subscript 2 reflects the square in its exponential.
X is the random variable being measured.
t is the strictly positive scale over which both norm infima are taken.
The Orlicz threshold 1 becomes the sub-gaussian exponential-moment threshold 2 after accounting for the minus-one term and E[1]=1.

undebatable_constraints: The selected function is exactly ψ₂(x)=exp(x²)−1 on [0,∞); the subtraction of 1 is essential.
The ambient space is a probability space.
The Orlicz norm uses an infimum over strictly positive scales t and the threshold E ψ₂(|X|/t)≤1.
The sub-gaussian norm in equation (2.13) uses an infimum over strictly positive scales t and the threshold E exp(X²/t²)≤2.
The equality of the two norms is exact, not merely up to an absolute multiplicative constant.
The corresponding finite-norm Orlicz space consists exactly of all sub-gaussian random variables.
No centering or mean-zero hypothesis is imposed on X for this definition or example.
The space claim includes every random variable satisfying any of the equivalent sub-gaussian properties (i)–(iv).

contract_plain_english: On a probability space, take ψ₂(x)=exp(x²)−1 for x≥0. The source explicitly says that this is an Orlicz function, that its Orlicz norm is exactly the sub-gaussian norm from equation (2.13), and that its finite-norm Orlicz space consists exactly of the sub-gaussian random variables. Indeed, the Orlicz condition E[ψ₂(|X|/t)]≤1 is exactly E exp(X²/t²)≤2 because P has total mass one, so the two definitions have the same admissible positive scales and the same infimum.
